dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses ISAM indexed files with ASSIGN to symbolic names, COPY with REPLACING using // delimiters, and .INC copybook extensions typical of ORCA system.
evidence: No EXEC CICS, no EXEC SQL, no COMP-3

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system - specifically point aggregation by diagnosis category for inpatient claims (入院 - 往診・自費請求)
purpose.summary: ORCR0840 is a batch program in the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system that aggregates diagnostic treatment points (診療区分別点数集計) for inpatient medical insurance claims. It reads multiple indexed ISAM files (RECE82, RECE84, RECE85, RECE8A, RECE8B) representing receipt detail records and writes aggregated point totals. It is part of the monthly receipt billing cycle for Japanese national health insurance.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY with REPLACING (37 COPY statements) for record layout reuse
Multiple ISAM indexed files with both DYNAMIC and SEQUENTIAL access modes on same physical file
Japanese EUC/Shift-JIS encoded comments (latin-1 decoded with mojibake)
Large OCCURS tables for day-by-day treatment tracking (WRK-DAY-TABLE, WRK-SKJ-TABLE)
33 CALL statements suggesting modular subprogram architecture
215 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
No COMP-3 packed decimal despite financial calculations (uses PIC 9 display numeric)
Error file (RECEERR-FILE) for batch error reporting
verdict.notes: File is encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS but decoded as latin-1, causing Japanese comment text to appear as mojibake. Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of 215702 bytes (4513 lines total); full procedure division not visible but structural indicators confirm complete 4-division COBOL program. The ORCA system is a well-known open-source Japanese medical receipt system maintained by JMA, strongly confirming GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL dialect on Linux.
